result:
The proposed construction does not avoid bowties, so the answer 0 is wrong.

In the construction, u is adjacent to v₁, v₂ in X and to every vertex of Y. Take two distinct vertices y, y′ in Y. Then u–y–v₁ and u–y′–v₂ are two triangles that share only the vertex u, which is a bowtie. The claim that there are no bowties checked only the bowties centred at vertices of Y, not those centred at u. The graph in fact contains many bowties centred at u, roughly on the order of q²·b².

The spectral comparison is also unjustified. Majorization of degree sequences does not imply a larger spectral radius, so the construction may not even satisfy λ(G) ≥ λ(K^q).

The extremal result this problem is based on says that any such graph must contain a positive number of bowties, growing with n and q. So 0 cannot be the correct answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
